summary: All eight implementations match independent comparison and array-change traces. The display counts swaps, except that merge sort counts single-item moves. The bar animation omits comparisons that do not change the array.

claims.claim: Bubble sort compares adjacent items in shrinking passes.
claims.how: It runs all shrinking passes, including any pass with no swaps.

sources.title: Bubble sort
sources.publisher: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures
sources.says: Bubble sort compares neighboring items and exchanges items that are out of order.

claims.note: All comparison values/operators and every array snapshot match the independent reference on 384 inputs.

claims.how: The last item is the pivot, values strictly below it move left, self-swaps are omitted, and left partitions run first.

sources.title: Quicksort
sources.says: Quicksort partitions around a pivot and recursively sorts the resulting subarrays.

claims.note: All comparison values/operators and every array snapshot match the independent reference on 384 inputs.

claims.claim: Merge sort combines runs bottom up and stably.
claims.how: Runs double in size. Equal values stay left; each needed right item is moved ahead of a left item.

sources.title: Mergesort
sources.says: Bottom-up mergesort combines adjacent sorted runs of increasing size; merge ordering can be stable.

claims.note: All comparison values/operators and every array snapshot match the independent reference on 384 inputs.

claims.claim: Insertion sort moves each new value into the sorted prefix.
claims.how: Adjacent swaps move the value left until it is in order.

sources.title: Insertion sort
sources.publisher: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures
sources.says: Insertion sort inserts each item into the sorted prefix; an adjacent-swap version is also described.

claims.note: All comparison values/operators and every array snapshot match the independent reference on 384 inputs.

claims.claim: Selection sort selects the minimum of each remaining suffix.
claims.how: It exchanges the selected minimum with the current destination, omitting self-swaps.

sources.title: Selection sort
sources.publisher: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures
sources.says: Selection sort repeatedly selects the smallest remaining item and moves it into place.

claims.note: All comparison values/operators and every array snapshot match the independent reference on 384 inputs.

claims.claim: Cocktail sort alternates forward and backward sweeps.
claims.how: Both sweeps shrink the active bounds and compare neighboring values.

sources.title: Bidirectional bubble sort
sources.publisher: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures
sources.says: Bidirectional bubble sort alternates forward and backward sweeps of adjacent comparisons.

claims.note: All comparison values/operators and every array snapshot match the independent reference on 384 inputs.

claims.how: Each gap performs insertion by exchanges within the interleaved subsequences.

sources.title: Shell sort
sources.publisher: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures
sources.says: Shell sort sorts interleaved subsequences at decreasing gaps, ending with gap one.

claims.note: All comparison values/operators and every array snapshot match the independent reference on 384 inputs.

claims.claim: Heap sort builds and drains a max heap.
claims.how: Heap construction starts from the last parent and repeated extraction moves the maximum to the sorted suffix.

sources.title: Priority queues and heapsort
sources.says: Heapsort builds a heap and repeatedly removes the maximum into the end of the array.

claims.note: All comparison values/operators and every array snapshot match the independent reference on 384 inputs.

claims.claim: The counter counts swaps or merge moves.
claims.how: For every recorded stage of all eight default traces, the seven-segment display shows the stage count and uses MOVES for merge, SWAPS otherwise.

claims.claim: Animated bar movements show only the exchanges or moves.
claims.how: Only changed arrays are saved; comparisons with no array change have no visible step. Merge insertion is one move, not a count of every write.

claims.note: The counter is not total running time, comparison count, or a fair memory-write benchmark across algorithms.

simplified: There are eight fixed bars in the picture. Comparison-only work is invisible. Merge counts one insertion move even when that move rewrites several array slots, so its counter is not comparable to a count of memory writes.

fixes.what: Make the About counter description say swaps, or moves for merge sort, matching the actual display.
